idea-plugin.name: Log Format String Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a log message whose placeholder count doesn't match its argument count -- a common bug that today only surfaces at runtime: a leftover placeholder stays literal in the log output, or an extra argument is silently dropped.

What triggers it:

  • SLF4J-style, Java/Kotlin -- log.info("User {} logged in from {}", userId, ipAddress): counts {} occurrences in the message literal and compares against the trailing arguments.
  • Python %-style logging -- logger.info("User %s logged in", user_id): counts %s/%d/etc. specifiers and compares the same way.

The SLF4J trailing-exception case, handled correctly: SLF4J treats a last argument as the exception to log (not a placeholder argument) when the call has exactly one more argument than placeholders -- the conventional shape log.error("Failed for {}", userId, exception) (1 placeholder, 2 arguments) is correct, never flagged.

What does NOT trigger it (tuned hard against false positives, see README for the full list): a message with no placeholders and no extra arguments, an exact placeholder/ argument match, the conventional trailing-exception shape above, and any case where the last argument's type can't be determined with certainty -- conservative by design, a missed real mismatch beats a false alarm.

Scope, honest about what's out: SLF4J-style Java/Kotlin and Python %-style logging only. Python f-strings are deliberately NOT scanned -- their interpolations are inline expressions, not separate arguments, so there's no placeholder-count-vs-argument-count mismatch to detect in the same shape (see README). Log4j2/structlog/Kotlin logging framework support and placeholder-type-mismatch detection are future work, not silently pretended to be handled.

Deliberately narrow: one specific pattern, near-zero configuration, tuned hard against false positives.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.

localInspection.displayName: Log message placeholder count does not match argument count
